correctness.rationale: For homogeneous intensities the maximum pmf is a Poisson pmf multiplied by a sum of synchronized powers of consecutive Poisson CDFs; the CDF is log-concave by its increasing cumulative-to-point-mass ratio, so the multiplier is log-concave. The exact Poisson recurrence transfers this to ULC. For unequal intensities the maximum pmf normalized by the largest-rate Poisson pmf has expansion m + s exp(b-a)(a/b)^k + o((a/b)^k). Its discrete logarithmic curvature has rigorously negative leading coefficient -m s exp(b-a)(b-a)^2/(ab), giving eventual strict failure. Boundary k=1 and all positive-rate cases are addressed; exact-rational verifier executed from the included code for diagnostic samples.

originality.rationale: The full 2023 Badiella–del Castillo–Puig paper proves ULC preservation only for iid sample order statistics, hence homogeneous sufficiency but not the unequal-rate necessity or curvature coefficient. The full 2021 Chowdhury–Kundu–Mishra preprint compares heterogeneous Poisson extremes in usual stochastic order, which neither states nor implies ULC. The inspected 2009 Yu paper uses relative log-concavity for stochastic comparisons and mixtures, not maxima with unequal intensities. Targeted published-finding corpus and public source searches, plus own prior claim comparisons, revealed no dominating theorem. Older alternative terminology remains possible; absence from searched records is not conclusive proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Alternative historical terminology (Poisson relative logconcavity, mixed-rate maxima) or unindexed earlier papers could contain an equivalent proof; independent priority confirmation is absent.
The full primary text of Kim et al. (2018) was not inspected; the cited 2023 paper identifies its scope as ordinary logconcavity of iid order statistics.
No direct comparison against private or unpublished research outside accessible records is possible.

value.rationale: Exact all-rate-vector rigidity sharply identifies the boundary of ultra-log-concavity preservation for a standard and naturally heterogeneous count-extreme family. The second-largest distinct rate and multiplicities govern a new explicit eventual negative curvature scale, which is more informative than a single counterexample; it is useful for deciding whether ULC-based shape/dispersion arguments can be transferred to unequal-rate Poisson maxima. No claim is made for ordinary log-concavity or a finite uniform transition threshold.
